facts.title: Night painted like weather of the mind
facts.body: Van Gogh’s Starry Night (1889), painted in Saint-Rémy, turns the Provençal sky into a living current of paint — cypress, village, and stars locked in one pulse.

facts.title: A dark flame to the sky
facts.body: The cypress rises like a black flame, bridging earth and the swirling heavens — a traditional emblem of mourning and eternity.

facts.title: Moon as a yellow sun
facts.body: The crescent moon burns with concentric rings of yellow — night lit as if from within.

facts.title: Venus before dawn
facts.body: The brightest “star” is often identified as Venus, the morning star Van Gogh watched from the asylum window.

facts.title: Impasto as wind
facts.body: Thick, curling strokes make the sky feel audible — turbulence you can almost hear.

facts.title: A quiet town below
facts.body: The village lies calm under the storm of sky — ordinary roofs against cosmic weather.

facts.title: A steeple from the north
facts.body: The church spire recalls Dutch architecture more than Provençal — memory layered onto place.

facts.title: The Alpilles rolling east
facts.body: Blue-green hills of the Alpilles roll under the night, anchoring the dream to geography.
